Write a natural short email exchange. Subject: Dinner. Participants: Me, Ben; Me is the owner's speaker label, not a spoken name. Date: 2026-10-06, local time 06:45–08:00.
Scenario: Ben's workweek has filled up. On Tuesday morning he emails from his desk asking to move their existing dinner later this week to another day. The user suggests Saturday and Ben accepts at the same time. Brief ordinary emails, without restating the restaurant or explaining app names.

The conversation must naturally and unambiguously establish each of these facts (they are authoring constraints, not lines to copy):
1. Ben and the user agree to move their existing dinner to Saturday at the same time.
2. The dinner’s venue is unchanged.
Use 2–12 short emails. The subject is header metadata; do not put a Subject: prefix inside an email body. Return only valid JSON with dialogue (a string with one Name: body line per email) and writer_note (a short string about the choices). No prose or Markdown fences outside the JSON.
